title: Smoke Hazards and Mitigation

nodes.text: Use lookouts to monitor and communicate hazardous smoke conditions. Make appropriate notifications

evidence.source_text: Use lookouts to monitor and communicate hazardous smoke conditions that may impact nearby roads. Make appropriate supervisory and/or safety notifications.

nodes.text: Rotate resources in and out of smoky areas. Consider exposure when developing mop up standards

evidence.source_text: If needed, rotate resources in and out of smoky areas. Consider exposure when developing mop up standards.

nodes.text: Ensure adequate rest and recovery from on-shift exposure to smoke

evidence.source_text: Ensure adequate rest and recovery from on-shift exposure to smoke.

nodes.text: Ensure adequate rest and recovery from smoke exposure. Avoid locating camps in areas where smoke can concentrate

evidence.source_text: Ensure adequate rest and recovery from on-shift exposure to smoke. Avoid locating fire camps in drainages, valleys, or low-lying areas where smoke can concentrate at night or under inversion conditions.

nodes.text: Provide mitigation for smoke exposure (e.g., clean-air sleeping trailer or hotel rooms)

evidence.source_text: If camps cant be moved, provide appropriate mitigation to ensure adequate rest and recovery from smoke exposure (e.g., clean-air sleeping trailer or hotel rooms).

nodes.text: Identify smoke sensitive areas and monitor smoke impacts

evidence.source_text: Identify possible smoke sensitive areas (roads, communities, schools, hospitals, etc.) that may be impacted by smoke. Monitor smoke impacts.

nodes.text: Notify authorities if heavy smoke is expected or present

evidence.source_text: When heavy smoke is expected or present, notify authorities such as the air regulatory agency, health department, or public safety, either directly or through dispatch.
